title: FancyZones Issue with msedge.exe Apps
summary: FancyZones treats distinct Edge PWAs as the same application for last-known-zone placement, matching the older open PWA support tracker.

status.label: Existing PWA placement tracker
status.detail: Open issue 652 already tracks supporting Chromium Edge PWAs separately for the last-known-zone feature, and closed issue 34713 was consolidated there with the same AUMID direction.

next_action.label: Post duplicate guidance
next_action.reason: Route the new Edge PWA details to the existing FancyZones PWA tracker instead of requesting a new diagnostic first.

judgment.rationale: The report describes the same FancyZones last-known-zone PWA identity problem already tracked by issue 652. The controlled diagnostic requested by the prior artifact would be useful for implementation, but under the current action taxonomy the maintainer-facing action is to consolidate with the existing tracker rather than split a duplicate issue.
evidence: The reporter has multiple Edge PWAs, and one PWA can open in the zone last used by another PWA.
The reporter specifically identifies shared msedge.exe or msedge_proxy.exe hosting and suggests Edge app ID or AUMID as the distinguishing key.
Issue 652 is an open FancyZones tracker for Chromium Edge PWAs and last-known-zone placement.
Issue 34713 described Chrome/PWA windows being treated as the same program, received an AUMID-based AppZoneHistory suggestion, and was closed as a duplicate of issue 652.
No assignee or linked PowerToys fix is present on the new issue.
judgment.recommended_action: Post a duplicate/consolidation comment pointing to issue 652 and ask the reporter to add any Edge-specific AUMID/window identity observations there.

issue_context.summary: Distinct Edge PWAs appear to share FancyZones last-known-zone placement state because they are hosted by Edge processes, a scenario already tracked for Chromium Edge PWAs.
known_information: The issue reproduces on PowerToys 0.100.2 on Windows 11 Pro 25H2 with three displays.
The reporter uses around a dozen installed Edge PWAs.
Different PWAs can open in the zone most recently used by another PWA.
Issue 652 remains open for FancyZones last-known-zone support for Chromium Edge PWAs.
Issue 34713 was closed as a duplicate of issue 652 and includes a concrete AUMID/AppZoneHistory direction.
inferences: The new report likely represents another instance of the existing PWA identity gap rather than a new standalone FancyZones regression.
The suggested AUMID or browser app ID evidence may be useful on the canonical tracker, but it is not necessary to keep this duplicate issue open.
issue_context.analysis: The live issue body supplies enough detail to match the existing tracker. Consolidating avoids duplicate design work while preserving the reporter's Edge-specific details as useful implementation context.
initial_investigation: Searched PowerToys issues for Edge PWA FancyZones placement and found issue 652 plus closed duplicate issue 34713.
Reviewed issue 652, whose comments discuss PWAs as browser processes plus per-window title identity limitations.
Reviewed issue 34713, where a commenter suggested reading PKEY_AppUserModel_ID for AppZoneHistory before the issue was closed as duplicate of 652.

actions.label: Close as duplicate of FancyZones PWA tracker

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed Edge PWA description and the AUMID/app-id suggestion. This matches the existing FancyZones tracker for Chromium Edge PWAs and last-known-zone placement in #652; a later equivalent Chrome/PWA report (#34713) was also consolidated there and includes the same AUMID direction. Please add your Edge-specific examples and any identity details to #652 so the implementation discussion stays in one place.

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.
